text:
sara (oncall): FYI customer ACME reported p95 jump ~2.3x right after the runtime v2.14 rollout at 17:05 UTC. Ticket #INC-12345.
sara (oncall): hitting p95 ~420ms -> 1.05s on their heavy chat workload, p99 also up but noisier.

mike (runtime): Did the canary show anything?
deploy-bot: rollout started v2.14 -> v2.15 across us-west-2, canary 5% at 17:00 UTC, 50% at 17:03 UTC, 100% at 17:05 UTC (release-id: r-2026-02-14-2145).
jia (perf): I ran historical queries against traces for cohort "acme-prod" — spike aligns with 17:05. Not seeing auth errors, just tail latency on token-fetch / kvcache lookups.
sara (oncall): repro steps from customer: 1) send chat payload with ~512 tokens, 2) model=redwood-1-large, 3) parallelism 12. They sent a curl that reproduces ~80% p95 bump.
sara (oncall): curl they used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" 
 -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","input":"<~512 tokens>","max_tokens":256}'
```

nora (support): attaching trimmed customer logs (from support-bot). support-bot: customer-log: request_id=abc-123 ts=2026-02-14T17:05:12Z kernel=quant-kernel-v3 queue_wait_ms=28 exec_ms=850 kv_hit=false
mike (runtime): exec_ms 850 is suspicious. Before rollout exec_ms ~320 for same kernel/cohort. What changed in v2.15?
jia (perf): v2.15 included a scheduler tunable and a small kernel selector heuristic change (prefer qkv-packed kernels for long sequences). Maybe selector now picks slower path for these inputs.
mike (runtime): I pulled the canary allocations — selector config diff:
```
- prefer: qkv-packed if seq_len >= 1024
+ prefer: qkv-packed if seq_len >= 256
```
mike (runtime): ah. that explains it — for seq 512 we now pick qkv-packed which is more memory-friendly but for this model+HW it runs slower on short batches.
sara (oncall): Customer workload is mid-size seq and high parallelism, so selector change could increase queueing + exec time.

nora (support): customer is blocked, wants ETA for mitigation.
jia (perf): Quick mitigations: 1) rollback kernel-selector heuristic in runtime to previous threshold; 2) route ACME -> fallback model variant (redwood-1-large-legacy) until patch; 3) reduce canary to 0% (partial rollback).
mike (runtime): we can hotpatch selector flag via feature-flag service. Patch plan: flip selector.threshold back to 1024 for all pods in us-west-2, monitor p95. Low-risk and fast.
sara (oncall): can you roll flag? If not, we need to rollback entire runtime version.
mike (runtime): I'll flip the flag now on canaries + 50% ramp bucket, then full region if metrics improve. Command:
```bash
rbctl feature set runtime.selector_threshold 1024 --env prod --region us-west-2
```
mike (runtime): executing...
mike (runtime): done. propagation ~30s.
jia (perf): monitoring cohort traces... p95 dropping from 1.05s -> 360ms within 2 minutes for sampled traces. p99 also trending down.
sara (oncall): forwarding fix and ETA to customer: patch rolled, observing improvements.
nora (support): sent update to customer, they confirmed initial tests look better.
sara (oncall): follow-ups: create postmortem item to revert selector heuristic until we validate per-GPU perf matrix. Also add a canary smoke test for mid-sequence workloads.
mike (runtime): I'll open PERF-456 to add per-arch kernel perf benchmarks and add an automatic canary check for p95 on representative cohorts.
jia (perf): Also recommend we add a runtime-flag guard to avoid switching to qkv-packed for parallelism > 8 or batch-size < X.
sara (oncall): Agreed. For now leave flag at 1024 and watch for an hour. If stable, close INC-12345 and schedule patch in next sprint.
mike (runtime): LGTM. Thanks for quick triage everyone. :thumbsup:
sara (oncall): closing loop with customer and sending brief incident note.
